prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: automated hospital medication dispensing/returns; goals timeliness, pharmacist oversight, traceability. Aliases: Medication Order Gateway=Morrowglass; Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot=Cinderwake; Pharmacy Verification Station=Juniper; Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler=Bluejay; Medication Return Kiosk=Tallowmere; Registered Nurse=Larkspur; Pharmacy Technician=Copperfield; Biomedical Engineer=Stonewake. Order Gateway validates orders, rejects incomplete updates with reason, routes to pharmacy review, produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Fulfillment Robot uses Snapshot to reconcile; stops pick/holds package on exception; no dispense before pharmacy authorization; produces Priority Refill Tote Tag (to North Ward Cabinet Controller). Verification Station: final checkpoint, holds mismatches, records approver/time/IDs, produces Batch Release Note (to South Ward Cabinet Controller). Medication Cooler: per-compartment temp limits, history with probe ID/calibration; excursion/probe loss makes stock ineligible, held; uses Cold Chain Handoff Card; logs access; offline alarms. East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles route via Pneumatic Tube Network (reconciled loads only; reports status/progress/delivery). East console routes by destination ID + approved config; stale/sensor loss→hold; logs interruptions; alerts Pharmacy Technician; sends Tube Route Exception Ticket (used by Biomedical Engineer). Cabinet Controllers: apply versioned approved config, check mapping/access rules/med classes; Ready for Dispense only after config checks+self-tests pass; Registered Nurse authenticates, selects order medication; controller checks authorization before unlocking; records user, order ref, compartment, time; high-risk extra confirmation; no config blocks dispensing. Modes: Ready for Dispense, Out of Service (on suspected fault/outage; remains until functional checks pass and staff approve return). Return Kiosk produces Return Bin Audit Label (to Pharmacy Technician). Clinical Pharmacist verifies orders, decides excursion disposition, keeps affected meds unavailable until checks repeated, produces Dose Exception Review Slip. Pharmacy Technician checks integrity/lot/expiry, produces Cold Chain Handoff Card. High-risk: independent second check. Medication Safety Officer reviews identity/access/risk discrepancies, sends Diversion Review Packet to IT Operations Specialist. Biomedical Engineer correlates records with telemetry, isolates subsystem, approved diagnostics only, records disposition/corrective action/evidence/approvals. IT Operations Specialist investigates auth/interface/time-sync faults; uses Cabinet Downtime Notice to open incident, checks status/network/logs, records detection time/equipment ID, isolates unavailable cabinet. Outage = no response, fault, or failed dispense

Document units:
S227: The Medication Order Gateway retains pending requests for review rather than treating an interrupted transaction as completed.
S228: The IT Operations Specialist checks whether any transaction was interrupted before the cabinet became unavailable.
S229: The Pharmacy Verification Station is used to confirm that pending medication orders remain valid before they are re-presented.
S230: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot is held from supplying medication to a cabinet that has not passed its recovery checks.
S231: The IT Operations Specialist coordinates technical troubleshooting with the Biomedical Engineer when equipment inspection or repair is required.
S232: The Clinical Pharmacist reviews medication orders affected by the outage when clinical validation is needed.
S233: The Registered Nurse uses the established clinical process for urgent medication needs while the cabinet is unavailable.
S234: The Biomedical Engineer reports completed repairs and any equipment limitations to the IT Operations Specialist.
S235: After repair, the IT Operations Specialist verifies communications, status reporting, and cabinet transaction behavior under controlled conditions.
S236: The responsible staff confirm that no unresolved transaction could cause a duplicate or missed dispense.
S237: The cabinet remains Out of Service until required functional checks pass and the responsible staff approve its return to Ready for Dispense.
S238: The West Tube Dispatch Console uses the Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record to verify capsule identity and seal status before closing its dispatch-side handoff checks.
S239: The West Tube Dispatch Console records completion of its handoff checks only after the required dispatch data are consistent.
S240: The Pneumatic Tube Network remains under monitoring while dispatch service is being restored.
S241: The Hospital Courier confirms physical receipt through the established delivery process.
S242: The West Tube Dispatch Console retains the handoff completion status for operational review.
S243: The IT Operations Specialist monitors cabinet and tube service status for recurrence during the recovery period.
S244: Audit records retain timestamps, equipment identifiers, recovery checks, and disposition details to support operational review and investigation.
